newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-Portugal details state electricity firm sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Portugal details state electricity firm sale.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government fixed the amount of state electricity firm EDP to be privatised at 30 percent, with domestic investors to get the lion's share.

The government said on Thursday that some 61 percent of the 179 million shares to be sold at the privatisation this month, the largest yet carried out in Portugal, would go to the general public, company employees and emigrants.
The remaining shares, which will be offered at between 1,750 and 2,250 escudos per share, will be sold directly to institutional investors such as banks and investment funds in Portugal and abroad.
The 30 percent assumes that the so-called green shoe, a reserve of shares at the disposal of the placement consortium, is fully exercised by institutional investors.
"The aim is not just to reach out to the small saver...but also to use the operation as a showcase for the economic situation in Portugal," Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco told journalists.
The government should raise between 313 billion and 400 billion escudos ($1.8-2.3 billion) from the sale for which subsciptions open on June 9.
The final price and individual allocations of stock will only be announced at a special bourse session set for June 16.

Requests for shares in the company, which made a net profit of 81 billion escudos in 1996, have so far exceeded the amount on offer by around 20 times during the pre-registration period when investors can indicate their interest in buying stock.
Sousa Franco said that the heavy demand was an indication of the "confidence in the economic stability of the country, the programme of privatisations and the quality of the company."
The some 100 million shares to be offered to the general public will include some six million shares for company employees.
The government plans to give a special bonus of one additional share for every 25 held for those investors who keep their stock for at least a year after the sale.
Bourse analysts expect the sale of EDP to help galvanise international interest in the Lisbon bourse which has been one of Europe's best performers over the past two years.

The widely-watched Morgan Stanley Capital International index (MSCI), the international investors' Bible, recently said it was upgrading the Portuguese stock market from emerging to developed, partly in response to the sharp growth in liquidity brought about by the government's privatisation programme.
